messages:
sarah-nguyen: Hey support, Lantern (tenant) reports sudden P99 spikes and intermittent 429s starting ~03:09 UTC on their Dedicated pool in eu-west. They9re pinned to a 7g MIG slice. Any takers?

kyle-ops: I9ll investigate. Do you have an example request id or timestamp?

sarah-nguyen: req_20260324_03:12:45_7b9f and customer traces showing many timeouts and 429s during 03:08-03:20. P95 fine, P99 up to ~4.5s for short responses.

mike-ortega: quick infra check: host euw-ded-13 shows SM util spike 03:08-03:18. MIG layout on that node: 1g/5g/7g. The 7g slice SM util hit ~97-99%.

anita-cho: Lantern is on the 7g slice there yes. Other tenants on 1g slices had heavy batching earlier. Could be L2/L3 cache thrash or KV-cache eviction from memory pressure.

kyle-ops: autoscaler logs show a scale decision at 03:05 to add capacity but action was blocked due to cooldown. Paste: ```[03:05:12] scale_decision: need +2 GPUs
[03:06:00] scale_action: throttle due to cooldown (remaining 600s)```

sarah-nguyen: So autoscaler cooldown prevented timely scale -> runtime hit soft concurrency limits -> returned 429s? Or runtime queued causing latency?

mike-ortega: Both. When SM saturates kernel queueing increases and we apply per-tenant soft concurrency reductions to avoid overload, which manifests as 429s. Need to confirm KV eviction events too.

infra-bot: capture: node=euw-ded-13, host_cpu=34%, gpu_mem_used=81%, sm_util=97.8%, nvlink_bw=normal

anita-cho: Repro plan for staging: 1) allocate a 7g-style slice on staging hw; 2) run many short clients (100-150 concurrent) pumping tiny prompts; 3) monitor p95/p99, kernel queue depth, and KV eviction rate.

mike-ortega: Repro done on staging: client concurrency=120, model=small-ctx-1, seq=64. Observed p99 ~3.7s, kernel logs show kernel-queue-depth spikes and stalls. Logs: ```kernel-queue-depth=256 stalls=412```

sarah-nguyen: Customer traces include repeated KV-cache misses causing recompute of prefixes. That aligns with memory pressure / eviction.

kyle-ops: MIG slice mem charts show transient spikes on sibling slices due to batching, total mem usage ~88%. This could have forced our runtime to evict KV pages for Lantern.

anita-cho: Short-term mitigations: - migrate Lantern off euw-ded-13 to a less noisy host (manual affinity) - apply temporary host-level concurrency override to lower tenant concurrency - consider emergency scale-up override when sm_util>90% for sustained window

sarah-nguyen: Lantern prefers no downtime. Can we do live migrate and warm up on new host? How long?

kyle-ops: We can perform a drain and reschedule to another host in the pool. Estimated time 8-12 minutes to move and reattach state. Need Lantern approval.

mike-ortega: Also proposing a 15-20m host override: tenant concurrency 32->24 on euw-ded-13 to reduce queueing and prevent cascading 429s while we move them.

anita-cho: Long term: autoscaler change request to ignore cooldown if sm_util>92% and p99 latency rising for >1m; add per-MIG memory watermark alerts to preempt KV eviction.

sarah-nguyen: @lantern-support: We'll migrate you now and apply a temporary concurrency cap. ETA ~12m. Sorry for the impact; we'll provide logs/traces afterward.

lantern-support: Please include KV cache eviction traces and any timestamps for our audit. User impact began ~03:09 UTC. Thanks.

kyle-ops: Actioning: drain euw-ded-13, evict Lantern pods, reschedule to euw-ded-21. Applying host-concurrency-override=24 (20m).

infra-bot: action note: drain started 03:19:42, evicting 4 pods, reassignment complete 03:27:10

mike-ortega: Post-migration: Lantern p99 dropped to ~210ms, no 429s observed 03:28-03:40. SM util on new host ~46%. All good so far.

sarah-nguyen: I'll close the support ticket after we hand off logs. Opening infra ticket for autoscaler heuristic.

kyle-ops: Filed INFRA-1721: "Autoscaler emergency scale when SM util high and latency rising". Assign infra squad.

anita-cho: I'll draft a short ops doc with recommended per-slice memory watermarks and alert thresholds for cross-MIG eviction risk.

sarah-nguyen: Thanks team. Tagging follow-ups: @kyle-ops, @mike-ortega, @anita-cho. :thumbsup:
